s1.syndrome_frame: Acute cardiac syndrome with inflammatory and thrombotic features
salient_findings: Elevated cardiac markers (troponin and brain natriuretic peptide)
key_facts: 47-year-old man with no significant medical history
Exposure to COVID-19 through family member 12 days before death
Developed general malaise without fever or respiratory symptoms 2 days before death
Fatigue worsened over time, and patient was unable to eat the day before death
Patient was not vaccinated
Cardiopulmonary arrest occurred during transport to hospital
No coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis was observed
Elevated inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-6)
SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive (>5000 pg/mL) from oropharyngeal swab
Postmortem CT scan showed dorsal pulmonary infiltrative shadow and bilateral pleural effusions
Pericardial effusion of 70 mL clear fluid
Heart weight was 426g, above normal range
Lung weights were above normal range

shortlist.label: COVID-19 associated myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive and cardiac involvement

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pericardial effusion and elevated cardiac markers

shortlist.label: Myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac markers and cardiopulmonary arrest

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Cardiopulmonary arrest and absence of coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient's recent exposure to COVID-19, lack of vaccination, and presence of SARS-CoV-2 antigen with elevated inflammatory cytokines support this diagnosis. The histological finding of diffuse contraction band necrosis and platelet aggregation in cardiac microvessels further suggests myocardial involvement due to COVID-19.

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: While pericardial effusion is present, the primary findings suggest myocardial involvement rather than a combined myopericarditis.

rejected.label: Acute pericarditis
rejected.why: The presence of pericardial effusion is noted, but the key findings of elevated cardiac markers, diffuse contraction band necrosis, and myocardial involvement point towards a more direct myocardial pathology.

rejected.label: Myocardial infarction
rejected.why: No coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis was observed, making a typical myocardial infarction less likely.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The direct evidence of COVID-19 infection and its effects on the heart, such as elevated cardiac markers and specific histological changes, make stress cardiomyopathy a less likely primary diagnosis.
